l: A. This General Order establishes guidelines for the safe operation of police vehicles and departmental procedures for responding to emergency and non-emergency calls for service.

B. These procedures must be viewed as an administrative guide for decision-making before the fact and as a standard for administrative judgment of the propriety of actions taken relating to emergency vehicle operation.

C. All personnel operating city-owned or leased vehicles for police operation shall exercise due regard for the safety of all persons. Criminal apprehensions and the preservation of property are secondary to the preservation of life. All department personnel who operate police vehicles will comply with the safe driving procedures outlined herein with particular attention to the procedures when responding to calls for service. Emergency warning devices shall be used consistent with both Texas statute and the safety of the public and police personnel. TBP 7.15

D. Emergency vehicle operations, especially those of sustained duration such as vehicle pursuit, demand a great deal of skill, common sense, and judgment on the part of involved officers and supervisors. During emergency vehicle operations, officers must consider the limitations set forth in the Texas Transportation Code, relating to officers’ legal responsibilities and be cognizant of and conform to the procedures and guidelines regarding emergency vehicle operations as established by this order. Especially during a vehicle pursuit, there is an overriding expectation that all officers must continuously weigh the gravity of the offense against the potential dangers posed to themselves and others. If officers elect to initiate or continue a pursuit, officers must function safely and effectively in an environment where far-reaching civil and personal consequences may hinge upon the soundness of split-second decisions.

E. Texas Transportation Code, Chapter 546 specifies that, provided the emergency lights and siren are activated, the driver of an authorized emergency vehicle when responding to an emergency call or in pursuit of an actual or suspected violator of the law may: TBP 7.15
1. Park or stand, irrespective of another provision of the Texas Transportation Code, Chapter 546.
2. Proceed past a red or stop signal or stop sign, after slowing as necessary for safe operation;
3. Exceed the maximum speed limit, except as provided by an ordinance adopted under Texas Transportation Code, Section 545.365, as long as the driver does not endanger life or property; and,
4. Disregard a regulation governing the direction of movement or turning in specified directions.

F. Despite legal authority to drive contrary to regulatory codes, negligent or reckless actions committed by officers during pursuit of actual or suspected violators or in responding to emergencies are prohibited by law. The authority to drive contrary to regulatory codes does not relieve a police officer from the duty to operate the vehicle with appropriate regard for the safety of others or the consequences of reckless disregard for the safety. TBP 7.15

a. Although state law permits a driver of an emergency vehicle to proceed past a red traffic signal or stop sign, when responding in an emergency manner and prior to entering an intersection and disregarding a stop sign or red traffic signal, Fort Worth Police Department personnel shall:
(1) Slow to a speed to ensure safe operation,
(3) Use extreme caution to ensure an intersection is clear and that any and all oncoming traffic has stopped or yielded.

b. Officers, whether driving in an emergency or non-emergency manner, shall come to a complete stop when a school bus flashes its red signal lights and activates its side stop signal. After stopping, the officer may pass the school bus only after exercising due diligence and extreme caution for the safety of the students in a manner that will not risk the safety of the students.
c. The monitoring supervisor will evaluate whether a pursuit should continue when pursued actors approach a densely populated area or active school zone.

d. Officers will keep in mind that traffic regulations requiring other vehicles yield the right of way to any emergency vehicle do not relieve the officer from the duty to drive with due regard for the safety of all persons using the streets or highways. The regulations do not protect drivers from the consequences of an arbitrary exercise of such right of way; therefore, right of way cannot be assumed or taken.
(1) Pedestrians are considered to have the absolute right of way.
G. The discretionary use of emergency lights and/or sirens is strictly prohibited unless expressly authorized according to Sections 305.02. TBP 7.15

H. Personnel shall not operate any city-owned or city-leased vehicle on official authorized city business when they are required to take medication that may impair their ability to safely operate a moving vehicle. Personnel have an affirmative duty to report to their health care provider that they are required to drive for city employment and the type of vehicles they are responsible to operate to enable their provider to give appropriate direction about the use of prescription medication and city driving tasks. Personnel must report any restrictions and limitations to their supervisor when taking such medication; however, personnel are not required to disclose the name of the medication or any medical condition warranting the use of the medication. This designation is used to describe the operation of a vehicle while the emergency lights and siren are activated. Officers will respond to the call immediately, using appropriate emergency equipment. Officers will operate a vehicle in Code 3 response with appropriate regard for the safety of all persons. Officers should proceed safely, drive reasonably for the conditions, and remain watchful of other drivers while driving defensively. Operation of a vehicle in a Code 3 response is permitted under certain circumstances as allowed by law; however, the actions of Fort Worth police officers are governed and limited by this order. Any Code 3 operation conducted in a manner inconsistent with this order may be contrary to law, may place the City of Fort Worth at risk of civil liability and may subject the officer to civil liability, criminal liability, and/or disciplinary action.
A. Examples of Code 3 calls include, but are not limited to:
1. Any Priority 1 call for service dispatched by police radio or initiated by an officer for serious crimes in progress or emergencies creating an imminent threat to human life and/or public safety.

2. For certain Priority 1 calls for service, such as barricaded persons, hostage situations, major disturbances, or riots, officers may be required to discontinue the use of emergency lights and sirens when approaching the scene. Although this action is permissible, once visual and audible emergency warning signals are discontinued, officers must return to Code 1 driving mode.
B. When operating in Code 3 mode, officers shall:
1. Yield and use extreme caution at stop signs and red-light traffic signals to ensure the intersection is safe and clear.
2. Not exceed the posted speed limit in active school zones.

3. Not exceed the posted speed limit by more than twenty (20) miles. If road, weather or other conditions are unfavorable and create a potential hazard, officers shall adhere to the posted speed limit and adjust their driving accordingly.
4. Although, under certain circumstances, an officer may be authorized to engage in Code 3 mode, prior to engaging in this mode, officers shall consider:
a. The distance they are from the incident,
b. The number of police units in closer proximity to responding,
c. Weather and road surface conditions,
e. The proximity of children and schools, and
f. An honest assessment of the officer’s driving skill level.
NOTE: Recognizing that the protection of human life is paramount, responding officers shall reach the scene as quickly as possible while ensuring and prioritizing the safety of themselves and others.
C. Code 3 operation is subject to the following limitations and restrictions:
1. The driver must be a commissioned peace officer.
2. The vehicle must be a marked police unit.

a. SWAT team members are exempt from the marked unit restriction when responding to known hostage situations, active gunfire, or other special situations approved by a supervisor, in accordance with the SWAT SOP.
3. The vehicle shall be operated with both emergency lights and siren activated.
4. Officers shall immediately notify the dispatcher when a Code 3 response is initiated.
5. Officers shall not operate a vehicle in Code 3 mode when any passenger is present, other than another Fort Worth police officer or a citizen who has signed a waiver of liability.
6. If the emergency call appears to be under control, but additional units are requested to continue, all other responding units shall continue Code 1 to the incident.
7. If the call is declared “unfounded” by any unit on scene, all responding units shall return to Code 1 operations and resume patrol.
D. Code 3 operation shall be limited and terminated as soon as practical.

1. Field supervisors, District/Section Lieutenants, and Midnight Duty Lieutenants shall monitor emergency vehicle responses, adjust response levels as appropriate, control the number of units responding, and return all available units to service as soon as possible.

2. Field supervisors, District/Section Lieutenants, and Midnight Duty Lieutenants shall intervene when necessary to coordinate the response of sufficient units, minimize risk to officers and the public, and ensure patrol resources are not unnecessarily depleted during a Signal Zero or any other emergency call for service.

3. As appropriate, Field supervisors, District/Section Lieutenants, and Midnight Duty Lieutenants shall provide feedback to responding officers. The officer’s chain of command will determine the appropriate course of action to address any violation of this order.
4. Officer Shot or Severely Injured Calls

a. Officer down or officer in trouble calls will be dispatched as a Signal Zero (0). If circumstances do not allow for the communication of a Signal Zero, the distress word, “Panther,” will have the same meaning.
b. Field supervisors shall respond to the scene of all Signal Zero (0) calls.

c. If an officer is shot or seriously injured in the line of duty, a mass response by units inhibits emergency medical personnel from responding to the location and/or inhibits emergency units from leaving the scene with injured officers. To better serve seriously injured officers, increase the likelihood of immediately apprehending the offenders, and maintain an acceptable level of police protection throughout the entire city, the following protocols shall be followed:

(1) Upon a Signal Zero call, where an officer has been shot or severely injured, the first supervisor on the scene shall notify dispatch if additional equipment and/or personnel are needed. If so, all responding units shall proceed to the incident Code 3.

(2) As soon as possible, the first supervisor on scene shall notify dispatch of designated ingress and egress routes for responding authorized emergency vehicles and identify a staging area for responding emergency vehicles to keep those routes clear.

A. Vehicular pursuit of fleeing suspects can present a danger to the lives of members of the public, officers, and suspects involved in the pursuit. Prior to engagement of a pursuit, the officer shall determine whether the pursuit itself will bring a greater risk of harm to persons and property than the loss of the suspect and whether the apprehension of the suspect by other means is possible. Although officers are not relieved from the responsibility of operating their vehicle in a safe manner, the operation of the police vehicle involved in a pursuit shall not be bound by General Order 305.02, Code 3 Emergencies which governs code three (3) responses.
1. Pursuit - A vehicular or motorcycle pursuit.

2. Vehicular pursuit - An active attempt by an officer in an authorized emergency vehicle equipped with emergency lights and siren to apprehend a fleeing suspect who is also in a motor vehicle and is attempting to elude the officer.
3. Motorcycle pursuit - An active attempt by an officer to apprehend a fleeing suspect, when either the officer or the suspect is on a motorcycle.

4. Fleeing - A suspect is considered to be fleeing upon making any overt action intended to avoid arrest. For the purpose of this order, violators who follow all traffic regulations after an officer initiates a traffic stop and are merely failing to yield to the authorized emergency vehicle are not considered to be fleeing.
5. Authorized emergency vehicle - A marked police department vehicle equipped with operable emergency equipment (i.e. emergency lights and siren) as designated by state law.
6. Primary pursuit unit - The police unit that initiates a pursuit or any unit which assumes control of the pursuit.
7. Secondary pursuit unit - Any police unit that becomes involved as a backup to the primary pursuit unit and follows the primary pursuit unit at a safe distance.

8. Designated supervisor - The field supervisor or lieutenant contacted and briefed regarding the pursuit by dispatch who will be expected to make decisions related to the pursuit. There will only be one designated supervisor per pursuit, unless one designated supervisor is relieved of the duty by another supervisor. The designated supervisor shall adhere to all responsibilities assigned in this General Order. Failure to follow the assigned responsibilities shall be considered failure to supervise with the supervisor being subject to discipline. Failure to acknowledge a pursuit by an on-duty field supervisor assigned to the division where the pursuit was initiated, regardless of whether the initiating officer is a direct report, may also constitute failure to supervise.

9. Violent offense - Includes offenses in which the suspect inflicted bodily injury, serious bodily injury, or death upon another individual. Violent offenses also include offenses in which the suspect uses, or threatens another with, a deadly weapon.
a. Violent offenses do not include assault by contact or offenses in which a suspect verbally threatens another without the apparent means to imminently carry out that threat.
1. The decision to pursue must be based upon facts and circumstances known to the officer at the time the officer begins the pursuit.

2. Officers shall refrain from initiating pursuits that shall create a greater harm to innocent bystanders or property than is warranted. In deciding whether to pursue, an officer shall consider the following pursuit risk factors:
a. Road, weather and environmental conditions;
b. Population density, vehicle and pedestrian traffic;
c. Relative performance capabilities of both the authorized emergency vehicle and the suspect’s vehicle;
e. Presence of non-sworn persons in the police vehicle;
f. Presence of other persons in the suspect’s vehicle;
g. Geographical area increasing risk to citizens such as residential areas, schools, or heavily commercial area;
h. Whether or not the offender’s identity is known; and
i. Any circumstance under which the pursuing officer will be unable to maintain control of the emergency vehicle.
2. The emergency warning lights, siren, and emergency vehicle headlights shall be used at all times during a pursuit.
3. The in-car audio/video system shall be used at all times during a pursuit, if the vehicle is so equipped.

4. Only marked police vehicles equipped with mounted operable emergency warning lights and sirens will participate in a pursuit. Supervisors in unmarked vehicles may follow the pursuit using a Code 1 response.

a. Motorcycle units that initiate or become involved in a pursuit as authorized in the above section, 305.03 (C 4 a) shall relinquish their position as primary pursuit unit as soon as a marked police vehicle is available to take over as primary pursuit unit. Upon the arrival of a second marked police vehicle to serve as a pursuit unit, the motorcycle unit shall disengage from the pursuit.

5. Supervisors may initiate a pursuit, but shall relinquish their position as the primary pursuit unit as soon as another patrol unit is available to take over. Dispatch should facilitate this change.
6. Upon engaging in a pursuit, the officer shall notify the dispatcher of the following:
a. Unit number and type (i.e., motorcycle or automobile) of primary pursuit unit;
b. Location and direction of travel;
d. Any relevant road/weather conditions; and
e. Description of the pursued vehicle and number of occupants.
f. If the pursuing officer is unable to provide the information listed above, the supervisor shall terminate the pursuit.

8. Upon initiation of a pursuit, police communications shall ensure that a field supervisor, District/Section Lieutenant, or Midnight Duty Lieutenant from the division in which the pursuit is occurring is immediately notified over the radio and briefed regarding the circumstances surrounding the pursuit. This person shall serve as the designated supervisor for the duration of the pursuit, unless relieved of the duty. If no field supervisor from the initiating division responds, Communications shall brief a field supervisor, District/Section Lieutenant, or Midnight Duty Lieutenant from an adjacent division and request that they switch radio channels to assume supervisory responsibilities of the pursuit.
a. The designated supervisor shall, as soon as they are briefed on the information contained in General Order 305.03(F) (6) above, announce over the radio their determination regarding whether:
(1) The pursuit is authorized and may continue, or
(2) Officers should immediately discontinue the pursuit.

9. Officers shall approach all intersections with caution. Although Texas law requires motorists to yield to emergency vehicles, officers should not assume that motorists see or hear the emergency vehicle until they actually yield.

a. When an officer approaches an intersection with a traffic control device that would normally cause traffic to stop at the intersection, the officer shall not proceed through the intersection until the officer can determine it is safe to do so. This can include:
(1) Being able to see that the intersection and all lanes of traffic are clear and no oncoming traffic will be encountered in the intersection, or
(2) Information relayed by radio from ground units or air units.
(3) If any vehicle(s) is in the intersection, the officer shall stop and wait until the intersection is cleared.

10. When any officer becomes aware that a hostage or other innocent passenger is or may be in a pursued vehicle, the dispatcher shall immediately be advised. All available information shall be reported including a physical description of the hostage, description of clothing and, when known, the exact location of the hostage within the vehicle, and any information regarding the suspects and weapons.
After being made aware of a vehicular pursuit, initiated either by Fort Worth officers or another agency, the designated supervisor shall:
1. Determine whether the pursuit will be allowed to continue;
2. Announce that determination over the radio;
3. Monitor incoming information that may affect the officer's determination about whether the pursuit should continue;
4. Immediately order the discontinuation of the pursuit when conditions dictate that such an action should be taken;
5. Coordinate and direct activities as needed to ensure that proper procedures are followed; and
6. Upon the termination of a pursuit, respond to the location where a vehicle has been stopped.
1. Upon notification from a Fort Worth officer of a pursuit situation, the dispatcher shall:
a. Close the radio channel related to the pursuit;
c. Notify, as applicable, the field supervisor, District/Section Lieutenant, Midnight Duty Lieutenant, and Air One;
d. Identify the designated supervisor for the particular pursuit;
e. Obtain the reason for pursuit; and and add them to the call sheet;
f. Monitor and broadcast pursuit progress.

g. When a pursuit enters into a different division, announce whether or not it has already been approved. Identify the designated supervisor by unit number or reiterate the need for a designated supervisor if one has not yet been assigned.
2. Upon notification from another agency of a pursuit situation that affects or will affect the City of Fort Worth, the dispatcher shall:
a. Notify, as applicable, the field supervisor, District/Section Lieutenant, or Midnight Duty Lieutenant, and Air One;
b. Provide the reason for the pursuit and any other details connected with the pursuit to the designated supervisor (i.e. suspect descriptions, weapons, charges etc.).
c. Monitor and broadcast pursuit progress.
3. Upon termination of the pursuit, the dispatcher will coordinate with the designated supervisor regarding the need for additional units and/or resources.

1. Safety of the involved officers, third parties, property and suspects is critical at the termination of a pursuit. The designated supervisor and primary pursuit unit shall continually re-evaluate and assess the pursuit situation, including all of the factors considered when initiating the pursuit, and shall discontinue the pursuit whenever the designated supervisor or primary pursuit unit reasonably believes the risks associated with continued pursuit are greater than the public safety benefit of making an immediate apprehension.
2. The pursuit may be discontinued by the primary pursuit unit at any time.
3. Any sworn Fort Worth Police Department supervisor of higher rank than the involved supervisor may order officers to discontinue any pursuit, at any time.

4. If non-uniformed officers respond to the termination point of a pursuit, they shall inform the dispatcher over the radio channel airing the pursuit, ensure they are readily identifiable as police officers by affixing proper identification to their outer clothing.
5. Upon termination of a pursuit, the location will be given over the radio.
1. Fort Worth pursuits outside of city limits:

a. When a pursuit leaves the City of Fort Worth (other than jurisdictions surrounded by the city limits of Fort Worth) and enters a county other than Tarrant County, a lieutenant or higher shall be notified to make the determination whether or not the pursuit will continue. That decision shall be announced over the radio.

(1) If a lieutenant or higher cannot be notified over the radio, the supervisor will continue to monitor the pursuit, attempt to notify a lieutenant or higher, and announce over the radio their determination regarding whether:
(a) The pursuit is authorized and may continue, or
(b) Officers should immediately discontinue the pursuit.
b. If the pursuit is authorized to continue, the unit broadcasting the pursuit shall advise the dispatcher of the jurisdiction being entered.
c. Before a pursuit enters another jurisdiction, or as soon as practical thereafter, the dispatcher shall attempt to notify the other agency of the following information:
(1) The pursuit is about to enter that agency’s jurisdiction;
(2) Reason for the pursuit and nature of the violation;
(3) Location and direction of the pursuit;
(4) Complete description of suspect vehicle and occupants;
(5) Number of vehicles/elements involved in the pursuit;
(6) Whether or not assistance is needed;
(7) If applicable, when the pursuit leaves that agency’s jurisdictional boundaries; and
(8) If within that agency’s jurisdictional boundaries, the location of the termination of the pursuit.
a. Officers shall notify the dispatcher when a pursuit by another law enforcement agency enters the City of Fort Worth jurisdiction.
b. Officers shall not join in a pursuit by another agency unless approved to do so by a designated supervisor.
c. A supervisor may join in a pursuit by another agency when the supervisor deems it necessary.

d. Upon notice that a pursuit initiated by another agency has entered the City of Fort Worth jurisdiction, the designated supervisor, contacted and briefed by communications as stated above, shall make a determination as to whether any participation by Fort Worth officers shall continue/begin, and shall broadcast that determination over the radio.

e. In the event a pursuit initiated by another agency terminates within the city limits of the City of Fort Worth, the agency with the highest charge involving the occupants of the vehicle shall be responsible for:
(1) Arrest and custody of the persons charged;
(4) Disposition of the arrested person’s vehicle; and
(5) Coordination of all reports related to the arrest, citations and criminal charges.
f. A supervisor shall make the scene of the termination point and ensure that all actions taken are appropriate and proper.

g. Any traffic collisions occurring within the city limits of Fort Worth as a result of a pursuit by another agency shall be worked by the Fort Worth Police Department Traffic Investigation Unit (TIU).
If a pursuit was initially authorized to continue by a supervisor, then the following apply:
1. Officers shall complete all necessary paperwork regarding the pursuit and any related offenses.
2. The designated supervisor shall respond to the termination point of the pursuit and ensure all necessary actions are taken and any required reports or notifications are made.
a. Review the offense report, generate the administrative pursuit report and forward the report to the proper chain of command for review or

b. Notify via email the direct supervisor of the primary unit initiating the pursuit, if the direct supervisor was on duty at the time of the pursuit, that the direct supervisor shall review the offense report, generate the administrative pursuit report and forward the report to the proper chain of command for review. The email notification must include a brief summary of the pursuit and the designated supervisor’s justification for approval.
4. If the chain of command identifies policy violations in the administrative pursuit report, discipline should follow the pursuit portion of the Fort Worth Police Department Discipline Matrix.
5. A copy of the administrative pursuit report shall be made available to the Driving Safety Coordinator to review for tactics training.

6. An annual report shall be prepared by Internal Affairs based on the data included in the administrative pursuit reports to identify trends and draw conclusions about safety or tactical improvement such as policy changes, training or equipment. The annual report shall be completed by the end of February for the prior year and directed to the Accreditation Program Manager.
